# A Brief That Manufactures the Average

**Niche:** [[niches/seo-tooling-vendors/content-brief-guidance/profile|Content Brief & Production Guidance]]
**Industry:** [[industries/seo-tooling-vendors|SEO Tooling Vendors]]
**Type:** Build (Greenfield Opportunity)
**One-liner:** Content briefs generated by tooling tell a writer to use a term nine times, hit 1,800 words and cover twelve subheadings taken from whoever currently ranks, which produces the interchangeable page everybody complains about.
**Tags:** #large-language-models #transformers #evaluation-metrics #word-embeddings #descriptive-statistics #confidence-intervals #revenue-impact #contrastive-learning
**Contested on:** Every serious competitor in this niche is fighting to guide a writer toward something worth reading rather than toward a statistical average of whoever currently ranks — and whoever does that stops the tooling from manufacturing the page everyone complains about.

## The Problem
The brief generator reads the ten pages currently ranking, averages their length, extracts their common subheadings and term frequencies, and instructs the writer to match. The writer produces a page that resembles the ten pages already there. It adds nothing, so it deserves nothing, and when it fails to rank the recommendation is to add more of what the average has. Every content team using this tooling is being guided toward the same output, which is why every result for every commercial query reads identically, and the category's own product is the mechanism producing it.

## Why Nobody Has Built This
Averaging the winners is easy to build, easy to explain and produces a score customers can chase, which is the product's appeal and its defect in the same sentence. What makes content genuinely good is hard to measure and harder to instruct. Customers ask for a checklist because a checklist can be assigned to a writer. And the convergence is a collective harm with no individual owner.

## What to Build
Guide toward contribution rather than conformance. Identify what the existing results fail to answer — the questions asked and unresolved, the contradictions between sources, the details nobody supplies — which is the core and turns a brief from a copy of the average into a specification for something new. Draw the gaps from real demand: the follow-up questions people ask, the community discussions, the support tickets, which are all obtainable and none of which the current generators use. Brief on the reader's situation rather than on term frequency, since who is asking and why determines what a good page contains and word count does not. Provide evidence requirements — what should be tested, sourced, measured or demonstrated — because first-hand substance is the durable differentiator and no averaging tool asks for it. Model what actually performed over time rather than what ranks today, connecting to the longitudinal corpus, since today's top ten is a snapshot and the corpus contains the trajectory. Score contribution rather than conformance, which is the fix note's subject. Brief for the generative surface too, where being a citable source depends on clarity and specificity rather than on length. Support the editor rather than replacing them, since the judgement about whether something is worth publishing is the part that should stay human. Warn when a topic is saturated and a new page adds nothing, which is genuinely useful and which no tool will currently say. And measure the outcomes of briefed content, because a guidance product that never checks whether its guidance worked is selling a ritual.

## Target Customer
Content teams and editors, SEO tooling vendors whose brief generators produce commodity output, and the agencies producing content at volume.

## Impact If Built
The tooling averages the winners and instructs the writer to match, which guarantees convergence and is the mechanism behind the sameness the category complains about. Briefing on unanswered questions and required evidence turns a copy of the average into a specification for something new.
